residents.name: Grandmother Cap's ring
residents.kind: a named Pokemon with a trap for a trigger: the folk tale is the warning
residents.situation: On the flat mushroom heath of the Fungal Isle's south half stands a perfect ring of red-and-white toadstools, ten blocks across, on a band of dark podzol. Inside it sit three more, small, and one big one. Islanders and ferry crews leave the ring alone, and someone has put up signs to say so. The big one is Grandmother Cap, an old Amoonguss who has sat in the middle of her own decoys for as long as anyone has rowed past. She is asleep until somebody steps over the ring: the trigger is the ring itself (trigger 9 against the ring's radius of 10), so the warning on the sign is exactly the rule.

residents.name: Post Fourteen and Ash
residents.kind: a named Pokemon left behind, its story told by the place alone: signs, a worn track, an empty post
residents.situation: On the flat top of Long Isle's north end stands a Haven Compact field post: a timber hut, a watchtower, and twenty blocks east of them a ring of smooth stone in the turf with a plank bar laid across it, the Compact's own field symbol (docs/story/FACTION.md: 'a plain open ring crossed by a short bridge'), and in its middle the stump of a field anchor (FACTION.md 'Method' 3: anchors define an exchange boundary). The crew went one night and did not come back. The sign by the door says relief was due in three days. The other says 'ASH: stay. guard. good dog. back soon.' Round the hut runs a perfect ring of bare trodden earth twenty-eight blocks across: Ash is a Houndoom and has walked that circuit every night since. Ash sleeps on the porch until someone comes within twenty blocks, and will not leave the post. Catching Ash is the only ending the place offers, and the only reward: somebody finally comes back.
residents.story_rule: nothing here says where the crew went, why, or what the anchor was for: the signs say only what a sergeant would write on a door. The arc's facts stay in docs/story/ (FACTION.md 'Method'); this place is consistent with them and reveals nothing they do not. Tier 7 and gated after gym 7, by when the player has met the Compact (docs/story/ARC.md, gym2_town)

residents.name: Tobiah Rusk's half-house
residents.kind: a story beat with nothing to fetch: one man, one strange fact, one question he asks you
residents.situation: In the open middle of Sunset Isle stands half a cottage. The west half is all there: walls, a gable roof, a door with a nameplate for two, a cold hearth, a bedroll, a lantern on a chain. The east half is not, and never fell down: the floorboards, the table, the rug and the roof all stop on one straight line, and the line goes on out of the house, a scar of bare earth and gravel running due north and south across the meadow for a hundred and twenty-nine blocks. Tobiah Rusk lives in the half that stayed. His wife Nell was in the kitchen, and the kitchen was on the other side of the line. He sets her place every night, and he will ask you one thing.
residents.story_rule: Tobiah does not know what an exchange is and never says the word; he says what he saw (a white light that stood along one line) and what he believes (a cut that clean moves people). That is the evidence every exchanged edge shows (docs/story/ARC.md, Pallet's 'localized damage where the exchange boundary closed badly'; docs/story/FACTION.md 'Method'), and nothing more. Sunset Isle is tier 8 (sunset_east), reached by the ferry, long after the player has heard the native account of displacement at gym1_town
